messages:
ivan: FYI I started seeing P2P throughput tank on a subset of A100 hosts after last night's kernel + driver canary. Latency up ~3x on multi-GPU jobs, NVLINK not showing up on some nodes.
marta: which kernel+driver combo? can you paste `nvidia-smi topo -m` from an affected host?
ivan: kernel `6.1.12-rt` + driver `530.41`. here's clipped output from one bad host:
```
GPU0    GPU1    CPU Affinity    NUMA Affinity
GPU0    X       PIX            0-15
GPU1    PIX     X              16-31

Topology: NVLINK missing between GPU0<->GPU1 (shows PCIe instead of NVLINK)
```
ravi: thanks. that's consistent with BAR1 window shrinkage + ACS isolation kicking in after the kernel's PCIe reconfiguration. saw similar on ampere in staging last month but not this widespread.
chen: ops-bot shows the canary pool had a mixed rollout across us-west-2 and eu-west-1 last night, but failure rate only in us-west-2. maybe a specific firmware combination?
ops-bot: deploy-bot: kernel-update `6.1.12-rt` rolled to cluster-canary-03 at 2026-03-17T23:10Z; driver `530.41` staged immediately afterward.
marta: if BAR1 is undersized the device apertures won't expose full BAR1 mappings and NVLINK can degrade to PCIe P2P; that explains perf. do we have dmesg logs showing BAR1 resize or IOMMU messages?
ivan: posted dmesg excerpt: 
```
[  25.432] nvidia 0000:65:00.0: BAR 1 size reduced from 256M to 64M
[  25.433] p2p: p2p link init failed, falling back to PCIe P2P
```
dave: immediate mitigation: mark affected nodes as no-schedule for large multi-gpu jobs, failover to canary pool with old kernel/driver. we can't afford broad rollbacks yet.
ravi: agree. also add quick eval: run `--topo-check` across nodes to detect NVLINK absence and add to evict list. script in infra-tools can do that.
chen: operational impact: us-west-2 capacity for multi-gpu training drops by ~18%, some reserved Dedicated customers will hit throughput SLAs. finance flagged potential credits if we stay degraded >24h.
marta: can we hotfix driver to force larger BAR1 via kernel cmdline `nvme_core.default_ps_max_latency_us`? (joking) seriously, there's a kernel param `pcie_acs_override` but it's risky. we should avoid hacks that break PCIe isolation.
ivan: current plan: 1) cordon affected nodes in us-west-2 2) revert driver on a small canary of affected hosts to `525.85` and validate NVLINK restored 3) collect `nvidia-smi topo -m` and perf numbers 4) if revert fixes, schedule staged rollback; otherwise escalate to HW firmware vendor.
ops-bot: action created INFRA-1298: "Investigate Ampere BAR1 shrink -> P2P fallback" assigned to eng-infra oncall.
dave: timeline? if revert works we can restore capacity in ~2h per rack, but we need ops approval for driver revert during business hours.
ravi: i'll run the revert on rack-canary-7 now and post results.
ivan: thanks. also enable detailed NCCL debug for one test job: `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0` capture logs so we can confirm switch from nvlink to pcie-p2p.
marta: note for postmortem: include cost delta from evicted jobs + potential Dedicated credit exposure. helps prioritize vendor escalation.
ivan: update: rack-canary-7 reverted to `525.85` and NVLINK restored, P2P throughput back to baseline in stress test. pushing metric samples to grafana under infra/ampere/p2p.
chen: great. follow-up: schedule firmware inventory across us-west-2 Ampere hosts and hold `6.1.12-rt` rollout until we confirm compatibility matrix with driver 530.41.
dave: I'll prepare a rollback playbook and cadence for safe staged driver upgrades + a topo-check preflight.
ivan: leaving here the quick commands we used: 
```
# topo check
nvidia-smi topo -m | grep -A2 GPU0
# revert driver (canary)
sudo apt-get install --reinstall nvidia-driver-525=525.85-1
# collect dmesg
dmesg | egrep 'BAR|p2p|nvlink' -n
```
ravi: ping me once playbook ready, i'll own the rollout validation. :thumbsup:
marta: thanks everyone. will draft a short incident note for customers and ops Slack with affected capacity and ETA. :memo:
